name: Legionarii Lanciarii seniores (palatina)

abilities.text: The troops of this unit raise their shields above their heads in a defensive formation.

abilities.text: The unit moves into close wall formation.

short: The Late Roman military system scholar, D. Van Berchem believes that in the 3rd century AD, along with the Praetorian Guard units, a new one appeared - the corps of Lanciarii. Based on the inscriptions, the Lanciarii were recruited from legion soldiers, and then served in the guard (sacro comitatu) for an undetermined period of time. The inscription «Maxentio aeq. ex numero lanciarorum (sic) vixit an. XXVI, mil. an. VI, iscola aequitum b. n. f.» indicates that Lanciarii were also present in the cavalry. At the end of their service, they were transferred to the Praetorian cohort or were given the title of protectors (protectores). If they had been in the Praetorian troops, they would have been disbanded together with them by Constantine the Great. Having outlived the Praetorian Guard, dissolved in 312 AD, the corps of Lanciarii took an honourable place in Constantine's comitatus. The Lanciarii participated in the battle of Adrianople as part of the field army of Valens II. When the battle took a dramatic turn for the Romans, the Lanciarii courageously fought to the last man, «as long as the numerical superiority of the enemy could be withstood» (Amm. Marc., XXXI, 13, 8-9). According to historians R. Scharf and E.A. Mekhamadiev, the terms seniores and iuniores reflected the process of gradual division of the late Roman legions, when from the ranks of the older legions, designated as seniores, were separated new units called iuniores. The formation of iuniores units allowed the sons of soldiers to begin their service in the same privileged military units in which their fathers (seniores) had served, and to advance up the military ranks relatively quickly.
history: In the face of an increasing number of barbarian incursions, the effective defence of Rome’s now-sprawling territory became a serious problem in the 4th century AD. The Emperor Constantine’s controversial solution was to divide the army into two halves. 'Limitanei', literally ‘the men on the limes’ or 'borders', were frontier garrison troops intended to pin down an invading force until the full-time 'comitatenses', the late-Roman equivalent of the traditional Legionaries, could arrive to deal with the situation decisively. Although well-equipped, limitanei were generally considered by all to be second-class warriors. This was possibly because they were often part-time soldiers who had been encouraged to settle and farm the land around their outposts in exchange for policing the Empire's borders.
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
